summary: Iteration 7 backend verification — 31/31 pytest tests PASS. Covered all new/changed endpoints: (1) /api/places/search (Nominatim OSM address geocoding) returns {results:[{name,lat,lng,display_name}]} for 'storgata 15 oslo', 'aker brygge', 'oslo lufthavn'; empty q or q<2 returns {results:[]} (never 500). (2) BUG FIX confirmed: POST /api/trips/request creates trip in 'searching' status; after 6s STILL 'searching' (no asyncio simulator). Only after driver /accept does it flip to 'driver_on_way'. (3) AI model switch to gpt-5.6-sol works: taxi-question returns Norwegian reply within timeout; off-topic 'skriv python-kode' → refusal starting with 'Beklager' (guardrails intact). (4) /api/pricing/surge returns {multiplier, reasons, active}; /trips/estimate 'enkelt' price matches expected formula (55 + 14*dist + 3.5*dur) * surge within ±2 kr; stacking is max() (not multiplication) confirmed. (5) POST /api/driver/trip/{id}/cancel works from driver_on_way AND in_trip → status 'cancelled_by_driver'; rejects 400 when searching (not accepted) and 400 after arrived. Push send call fires (no crash). (6) GET /api/driver/history returns {trips:[]} newest-first with only arrived/completed/rated/cancelled_by_driver statuses; no MongoDB _id leaked. GET /api/driver/history/weekly returns exactly 7 days with date/day_label/income/trips and total sums correctly. (7) Regressions PASS: auth/login, driver/online, driver/location, cars/nearby empty↔populated, trips/estimate, driver/pending, driver/accept, driver/trip/{id}/start, driver/trip/{id}/arrive, payments/checkout on arrived trip (+400 when not arrived), gdpr/export, gdpr/delete on throwaway user (login 401 after), admin/driver-invites with NEW schema {car,plate,vehicle_type,note,email}.

minor.issue: Response is {ok:true} without echoing new status. Frontend must re-fetch trip. Consider returning trip document for consistency with /driver/accept.
Uses .sort('created_at', -1) but stores created_at as ISO string; works because ISO 8601 strings sort correctly, but relies on that convention. Consider persisting as native datetime for safety.

created_at range filter uses date().isoformat() (10-char) compared against full ISO strings; string comparison works but is fragile — a created_at like '2026-01-05T23:59:59Z' correctly compares < '2026-01-06'. OK for now but tie to native datetimes for robustness.
No caching / rate-limit. Nominatim usage policy limits to 1 req/sec — under user typeahead load this may 429. Add debounce on frontend (already done per note) + optional server-side cache.

action_items: Consider returning updated trip document from /driver/trip/{id}/cancel for FE parity with /accept.
Persist trip.created_at as native datetime (BSON Date) instead of ISO string — future-proofs history queries and range filters.
server.py is now 1683 lines — split into modules (auth, trips, driver, admin, payments, ai, push, places, pricing) before further growth.
Add server-side cache/rate-limit for /places/search to respect Nominatim's 1 req/sec policy.
critical_code_review_comments: surge logic uses `(now.hour + 1) % 24` as a naive UTC→CET conversion; this is INCORRECT during summer time (CEST is UTC+2). During DST, a request at 21:00 UTC would map to local_hour=22 and trigger night surge, but actual local time is 23:00 (still night, OK). Reverse: 20:00 UTC maps to local_hour=21 (no night surge), but actual local is 22:00 (should trigger). Consider using zoneinfo('Europe/Oslo').
price_for/current_surge_info duplicate the same weekday+hour logic; refactor into a single _compute_surge(when) helper called by both.
/api/driver/trip/{id}/cancel push notification to passenger has no fallback — verified webpush fires; if user has no subscriptions send_push_to_user returns silently (good).
history_weekly loops per-day with N find() calls (7 round-trips). For a busy driver, use a single aggregate with $group by date. Not urgent for beta.
